card: Describe a colleague or fellow student you work well with.
pts: what kind of work you do together
and explain why you work well together
model:
I'd like to talk about a fellow student from my master's programme, whom I'll call my study partner. We both research topics connected to law and public administration, and we've been working together for about a year.

We met in the first week of the course, when the lecturer put us in a pair for a presentation on public procurement. At that point we hardly knew each other, but the presentation went so well that we decided to keep collaborating.

Nowadays, we share a lot of tasks. We read the same articles and then compare our notes. She is better at structuring arguments, whereas I tend to look for data and examples, so we cover each other's weaknesses. Before every deadline, we also read each other's drafts and give honest feedback.

What makes us such a good team is mainly trust. If one of us doesn't understand something, we say so immediately without feeling embarrassed. On top of that, we have similar standards: neither of us enjoys leaving things until the last minute.

I think this partnership has improved my work considerably. I used to be quite stubborn about my ideas, but now I'm more open to criticism. All in all, it's the kind of cooperation I hope to find in my future career as well.
phr: What makes us such a good team is...
tipAr: استخدم whereas وtend to لتُظهر مقارنة بين شخصيتين بأسلوب أكثر نضجاً، فهذا يرفع درجة التنوع في القواعد.

card: Describe a person you admire for what they have achieved.
pts: and explain why you admire them
model:
The person I'd like to describe is a scientist from my region who built her career in medical research despite very limited resources. I don't know her personally, but I've followed her story for several years.

She grew up in a small town without a proper laboratory, and she had to study in a second language. Even so, she won a scholarship, completed her doctorate abroad and later returned to open a small research unit at a public university. Her team has developed a low-cost test that helps clinics detect a common disease earlier.

I first heard about her in a documentary that a lecturer recommended in my first year. Afterwards, I read several interviews in which she spoke openly about failure, which I found very refreshing.

The reason I admire her is twofold. First, she was extremely persistent: she was rejected many times before her work was accepted. Second, she chose to share her knowledge rather than keep it for herself, training dozens of young researchers for free.

Her example shows me that talent alone is not enough; what really matters is patience and a sense of responsibility towards others. That's why she has become a kind of role model in my own academic journey.
phr: The reason I admire her is twofold.
rather than keep it for herself
tipAr: في وصف شخص تُعجب به، قدّم سببين واضحين (First... Second...) فهذا يمنح إجابتك بنية قوية ويسهّل عليك الاسترسال.

card: Describe a market or shopping place you have visited.
pts: and explain what you liked or disliked about it
model:
I'd like to describe the weekly market in a small town near my hometown. It takes place every Friday in a large open square, and people come from all the surrounding villages to buy and sell.

I went there last spring with my aunt, who wanted to buy vegetables and some fabric. We arrived quite early, at around eight o'clock, because she said the best products disappear first.

The moment we got there, I was struck by the colours and the noise. There were stalls with piles of oranges, fresh herbs and olives, and sellers were shouting prices to attract customers. Further along, there were stands for spices, second-hand books and even old tools. In the end, I bought a pair of leather shoes and a small bag of dates, and my aunt got a very good price for her fabric after some friendly bargaining.

What I liked most was the atmosphere. Everyone seemed to know each other, and there was a real sense of community. On the other hand, it was extremely crowded, and I had to watch my bag carefully. There was also quite a lot of rubbish on the ground by midday.

Overall, it was a lively and authentic experience, and I would happily go again.
tipAr: البطاقة تطلب ما أعجبك وما لم يعجبك؛ لا تنسَ ذكر جانب سلبي واحد باستعمال On the other hand لتبدو إجابتك متوازنة.

card: Describe a building you find interesting.
pts: and explain why you find it interesting
model:
The building I'd like to talk about is the old courthouse in the centre of my city. It was built during the early twentieth century, and it stands right next to the main square, so almost everyone passes by it every day.

In terms of appearance, it is quite impressive. It has a wide stone staircase, tall columns at the entrance and a large clock above the main door. The walls are a pale yellow colour, and the windows are decorated with iron patterns. Inside, there is a big hall with a high ceiling, which gives you the impression that justice is something serious and important.

Today, it is still used as a court, mainly for civil cases. A few years ago, I visited it with my class to watch a hearing, and that was the first time I saw a real trial.

The reason it fascinates me is that it combines history with something I'm really passionate about. When I stood in the hall, I tried to imagine all the people who had come there over the decades, hoping for a fair decision. It made me realise how much responsibility lawyers and judges carry.

To sum up, it's more than a beautiful structure; for me it is a symbol of the values I want to work for.
phr: it gives you the impression that...
The reason it fascinates me is that...
tipAr: ابدأ بالوصف المادي (الشكل واللون) ثم انتقل إلى الوظيفة ثم الأثر الشخصي؛ هذا ترتيب مريح للمستمع.

card: Describe a useful tool or piece of technology that you use regularly.
pts: and explain why it is useful to you
model:
The piece of technology I rely on most is my laptop, and more specifically, a note-taking application that I run on it. I use it every single day for my studies and my research.

I started using it about two years ago. A classmate showed it to me when I was complaining that my paper notes were completely disorganised. At first I was sceptical because I had always preferred writing by hand, but after a week I was hooked.

Nowadays, I use it for almost everything. I store my lecture notes, link ideas between different articles and keep a list of sources for my thesis. I can also search for any word in seconds, which is incredible when you have hundreds of pages. Besides, it works offline, which is essential where the internet connection is not always stable.

The main reason it's so useful is that it saves me a huge amount of time and reduces stress. Before, I would waste half an hour looking for a single reference. Now I find it in a few seconds.

Having said that, I try not to depend on it too much. I still write down my most important thoughts by hand, because I remember them better that way.
tipAr: عبارة Having said that مفيدة جداً لإضافة تحفّظ بسيط بعد رأي إيجابي، وتُظهر قدرتك على التفكير المتوازن.

card: Describe a competition or contest you took part in.
pts: when and where it took place
and explain how you felt about the result
model:
I'd like to talk about a university debate competition that I took part in two years ago. It was organised by the faculty of law and included teams from five different universities.

It took place over a weekend in a big lecture hall in the capital. My team consisted of three students, and I was the second speaker. Before the event, we had prepared for almost a month, meeting every evening after class.

The format was quite demanding. We were given the topic, whether public officials should declare their wealth, only fifteen minutes before each round, and we had to prepare arguments for one side, even if we personally disagreed. In the final round, I had to respond to the other team's points on the spot, which was extremely stressful.

As for the result, we came second. Naturally, I was a bit disappointed at first because we had been so close to winning. However, after a day or two, I realised how much I had gained. My public speaking improved enormously, and I learnt to listen carefully to opponents instead of just waiting for my turn.

Looking back, I'm proud of the effort, and I'm planning to take part again next year.
tipAr: عند الحديث عن نتيجة غير مثالية، اذكر شعورك الأول ثم ما استفدته؛ هذه التفاصيل تُظهر نضجاً في الإجابة.

card: Describe a memorable journey you made.
pts: and explain why the journey was memorable
model:
I'd like to describe a long train journey I took across the south of the country with two close friends. It happened in the summer after our second year at university, and we were heading to the desert region to see some historical sites.

We set off early in the morning, and the trip was supposed to take about ten hours. Unfortunately, the train broke down in the middle of nowhere, and we had to wait for almost three hours in the heat. At first we were quite irritated, but then some other passengers shared their food and tea with us, and the atmosphere changed completely. We ended up singing and chatting with strangers.

When we finally arrived, it was already dark. We went outside and looked up at the sky, and I had never seen so many stars in my life. The next day, we visited ancient rock paintings, which was the highlight of the trip.

The reason this journey stays in my memory is that things didn't go according to plan, yet it turned out to be better than expected. It taught me that unexpected problems can sometimes create the best stories, and that kindness from strangers can make a long wait feel short.
tipAr: الجمل مثل was supposed to وended up تضيف مستوى لغوياً أعلى؛ حاول استعمال اثنتين منها على الأقل.

card: Describe a difficult decision you made.
pts: when you had to make it
how you made up your mind
and explain whether you think it was the right decision
model:
The decision I'd like to describe is choosing to continue with a master's degree in a field that was not my original specialty. I had studied accounting and finance, so most people expected me to look for a job in a bank or an accounting firm.

I had to decide about a year ago, just after graduating. At that time, I'd received a small job offer, and the salary was reasonable. However, I had become more and more interested in transparency and the fight against corruption, and I knew that a master's in this area would give me a chance to do research.

To make up my mind, I did several things. First, I wrote a list of advantages and disadvantages. Then I talked to two lecturers and an older cousin who works in an office. In the end, my own curiosity decided it: I realised that I would regret it more if I did not try.

Looking back, I'm convinced it was the right choice, even though it hasn't always been easy. Money has been tight, and I sometimes doubt myself. Nevertheless, I'm learning things that truly motivate me, and I've found a clear direction for my future. That feeling is worth more than a quick salary.
phr: even though it hasn't always been easy
tipAr: عند الحديث عن قرار، اذكر الخيارات التي كانت أمامك ثم كيف رجّحت أحدها، وأنهِ بتقييم صريح فيه إيجابيات وصعوبات.

card: Describe a skill you learnt and are proud of.
pts: and explain why you are proud of it
model:
The skill I'm most proud of is programming, and in particular, writing small tools that automate repetitive tasks. I started learning it about three years ago, mostly because I was curious about how software works.

I learnt mainly by myself. I followed free video courses in the evenings and then tried to build small projects, like a script that sorts my files or one that checks a document for repeated sentences. Occasionally, I asked for advice in online forums, and people were surprisingly helpful.

That said, it wasn't always smooth. For the first few months, my programs kept crashing, and I couldn't understand the error messages. Once, I spent an entire weekend looking for a mistake, and it turned out to be a missing comma. I nearly gave up several times, especially during exams.

What makes me proud is that I've kept going despite those problems. Today, I can build useful tools that save me hours of work, and I even helped a friend organise the data for his thesis. Beyond that, it has changed how I think: I now break big problems into small steps.

In short, it's a skill that has opened many doors for me, and I'm still improving it every week.
tipAr: لا بأس أن تذكر الصعوبات والأخطاء الصغيرة؛ فهي تجعل القصة طبيعية وتمنحك مفردات إضافية مثل crash وgive up.

card: Describe a mistake you made and what you learnt from it.
pts: how you realised it was a mistake
and explain what you learnt from it
model:
I'd like to talk about a mistake I made while preparing an important assignment last year. I was asked to write a short report for a seminar, and I trusted a website that looked very professional without checking who had written it.

It happened about two weeks before the deadline, in the university library. I collected several statistics from that site and included them in my report without verifying them anywhere else. I was in a hurry, so I convinced myself that it must be correct.

I realised my error during the presentation. A classmate raised her hand and politely asked about my source. When I looked for it, I found that the website didn't mention where the numbers came from. Afterwards, the lecturer told me that two of them were completely outdated. I felt extremely embarrassed.

Fortunately, I learnt a great deal from this experience. Firstly, I now always check at least two reliable sources before using any figure. Secondly, I begin my assignments earlier so that I'm not tempted to rush. Finally, I understood that admitting a mistake openly is far better than hiding it.

In a way, I'm almost grateful it happened, because it made me a more careful researcher.
phr: It happened about... before the deadline
I learnt a great deal from...
tipAr: ختم الإجابة بما تعلمته هو الجزء الأهم في هذه البطاقة؛ خصّص له ثلث الوقت تقريباً واستعمل Firstly وSecondly وFinally.
